ruling: OWNER RULING 2026-09-25: ONE CANONICAL SANDBOX LOGIN PER CANONICAL JOB ROLE. Exactly one chain per role: Credential -> Auth account -> EOS Principal -> Employee -> Job Role. Security Roles stay SEPARATE from Job Roles; nothing here says what an identity may do, which is read from PostgreSQL at request time.
$whyThisFileExists: ONE AUTHORITY, TWO MODULE SYSTEMS. scripts/sandboxCredentials.mjs is ESM and functions/scripts/seedSampleCompany.js is CommonJS, so neither can import the other. Duplicating the registry in both is how the two would drift, and the symptom of drift here is an account created for an identity that already has one. JSON is the one shape both can read, so this file is the authority and both consume it. NO CODE MAY CARRY A COPY OF THESE ADDRESSES: the seed does one lookup against this file and holds no address literals, which is the failure mode the ruling explicitly forbids.
confirmedBy: Authoritative Firebase Admin SDK lookup against eos-platform-sandbox via ADC, 2026-09-25. 15 of 16 accounts exist; reporting@sandbox.invalid does not.
$uidNote: A uid is an IDENTIFIER, not a credential: it proves which account a key names without revealing anything that can be signed in with. It is also the only way to catch the defect that keeps recurring here -- a key whose address and whose uid belong to two different accounts.

credentialEmailInvariant.exception: A canonical role identity declared in `roles` below MAY have a credentialEmail that differs from the Employee's workEmail. employee.workEmail is business/profile contact data; loginPrincipal.credentialEmail is authentication identity. They are distinct concepts and the sandbox consolidation is built on that distinction.
credentialEmailInvariant.$notAGenericRule: This is NOT a general 'emails may differ' permission. The exception applies ONLY to a persona with an entry in this registry, and ONLY when the declared authEmail matches exactly. Any other divergence is still MANIFEST_INVALID.
conditions: the persona is in the canonical 16-role identity registry
the registry explicitly declares the canonical authentication email
that declared Auth email resolves to exactly one intended sandbox identity
no duplicate canonical persona uses that Auth identity
the Employee workEmail is left UNCHANGED
no Firebase business authority is created

$noncanonicalPolicy: RETAINED, NOT DELETED. The Owner ruled stale accounts stay until a separate cleanup wave authorizes deletion. None of these may appear in the canonical catalog, be required for browser acceptance, receive a duplicate EOS Principal, or drive role or security decisions. Recorded as DATA rather than prose because a comment cannot stop one being adopted, and adopting a plausible-looking fixture address is the exact mistake this registry exists to end.

$expectedSecurityRoles_comment: Declared ONLY where the Owner ruled one. null means NOT_DECLARED: step 9 of sandboxPersonaBootstrap reports what is held and raises no blocker, because an expectation this tooling does not have is not one it may invent. Security Roles are verified SEPARATELY from Job Roles and are never granted by the bootstrap -- it owns identity and Job Role, and a command that could also grant authority is a command that can quietly widen access to make its own report green.

applyPhases.$comment: The order an apply must follow. Each phase depends on the one before: an Auth account with no Job Role catalog to assign from is a half-built identity, and that half-built state is what this ordering exists to prevent.

1.name: AUTH
1.action: Ensure exactly one PASSWORDLESS sandbox Auth account per canonical role. Reuse every existing account; create only a genuinely missing one. Measured 2026-09-25: 15 exist, only reporting@sandbox.invalid does not.

2.name: JOB_ROLE_CATALOG
2.action: Seed eos_workforce.job_roles from 0 to 16 via the governed createJobRole. The ids come from lib/eosWorkforce/jobRoleVocabulary CANONICAL_JOB_ROLE_IDS, so a retired id and `field-trainer` are structurally excluded rather than filtered by hand.

3.name: EXISTING_PERSONAS_AND_OWNER_ADMIN_SPLIT
3.action: Reconcile the thirteen existing personas, and perform the Owner/Admin split: create the Administrator Employee, then relink the Owner/Executive Employee off the Admin Principal onto the Owner Principal with expected-current protection.

4.name: FINANCE
4.action: Reconcile financeAccounting against the EXISTING acctmgr@ account. Security Role expectation: accountingManager ONLY.

5.name: REPORTING
5.action: Create the ONE missing account, reporting@sandbox.invalid, then reconcile. Security Role expectation: reportViewer ONLY, and its capability baseline must include reportDefinition.read.

6.name: RESTRICTED
6.action: Reconcile generalEmployee against the EXISTING restricted@ account, Job Role general-employee, and ZERO Security Roles -- never the `generalEmployee` Security Role.

ownerAdminSplit.$comment: Measured: ONE Principal (the Administrator, firebase ZVu3lHTP...) is linked to the Owner/Executive Employee, and the Principal that actually holds `owner` has NO Employee link at all. So the Owner Executive persona currently signs in as the administrator, and the owner authority is unreachable through any Employee-scoped predicate. Splitting them is an ADD plus a MOVE, never a delete.
steps: createEmployee(administratorEmployeeId) -- the Administrator has no Employee of its own today
ownerAdminSplit.$expectedCurrentProtection: relinkEmployeePrincipal takes expectedCurrentPrincipalId, so the move is refused if the link is not where we measured it. That turns a stale observation into a refusal instead of a silent repoint onto the wrong Principal -- which is the whole class of failure this registry exists to end.

$expectedEmployeeId_comment: The Employee this canonical role is linked to. Declared so the bootstrap can detect an EMPLOYEE_PRINCIPAL_LINK_MISMATCH -- a Principal linked to some OTHER Employee is not a missing link, it is a wrong one, and the two need different fixes. ownerExecutive and administrator are named explicitly because they are the two REUSED real Principals and the Owner/Admin split moves one of them.
